I need the front end for Proofloop. A messaging tool for small data-visualization studios where client feedback, internal discussion and approvals are kept attached to the exact version of each chart or graphic they refer to.

Who's using it: Ines Varga, creative lead and co-owner of Fieldnote Studio, a seven-person data-graphics shop. She handles client relationships and does final sign-off on deliverables.

What they're doing right now: It's Monday morning. Overnight the communications manager at the Tri-County Transit Authority replied to version 3 of the ridership-recovery graphic. She wants the pandemic dip 'de-emphasized' and the y-axis to start at 40%. Meanwhile Ines's designer Kofi asked internally whether truncating the axis is acceptable, and the agency's data analyst separately sent a corrected October figure. Ines has to reconcile the three conversations, reply to the client with a position on the axis request and a proposed v4 date, and make sure Kofi gets the corrected data. She also needs to keep the internal debate out of what the client sees.

What's in the system at this point: Active project: 'Riding Back: 2019–2026 Ridership Report' for Tri-County Transit Authority, 6 graphics, due December 5. The ridership graphic has versions v1 (Oct 14), v2 (Oct 29) and v3 (Nov 12), each with an attached image and data file. Message history on this graphic: 34 messages across 3 conversations. The client conversation has Ines, project manager Dara Lin and the client contacts Renée Almeida (communications) and Sam Pruitt (data analyst). The internal-only conversation has Ines, Kofi Mensah and Dara. Sam's separate reply on Nov 15 corrects the October 2026 ridership figure from 81.4% to 79.8% of 2019 levels. Two messages are pinned to specific points on v3 (the April 2020 low, the axis label). The client still owes approvals on graphics 2 and 5. Other studio projects in flight: 4, with 11 unread client messages in total, the oldest from Thursday.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
